title: Probate Real Estate — Operator Companion Workbook
subtitle: 6 Printable Operator Worksheets for Probate Deal Qualification, Retained-Commission Economics, Executor Concierge Delivery, Court-Sale Controls, Attorney Referral Systems, and Small-Team Operating Readiness

worksheets.title: Opportunity Underwriting and Fiduciary Counterparty Qualification
worksheets.purpose: Select probate brokerage opportunities that fit the team's license, court experience, cash runway, and service capacity. Separate an estate's property value from brokerage revenue, establish who can instruct the broker, and expose title, authority, occupancy, and family conflicts before committing substantial work.
instructions: Choose one initial county and one service lane. Record the applicable probate court, supervising broker, property profile, and expected appointment-to-closing interval. Treat acquisitions and executor concierge work as separately contracted activities rather than automatic extensions of a brokerage listing.

Obtain the appointment documents and relevant orders from the authorized representative or court record. Have estate counsel identify the representative's powers, restrictions, and required sale procedure. Do not treat a relative's possession of keys as authority to list.

Build a counterparty map covering the representative, estate attorney, beneficiaries, occupants, lender, title officer, and prospective buyers. Distinguish decision authority from consultation preferences, and document the permitted recipients of confidential pricing, offer, and estate information.

Underwrite property condition, liens, occupancy, access, insurance, and carrying costs before projecting commission timing. Use a dated comparative market analysis and scenario ranges. Track potential family objections as procedural and scheduling risks, not as presumed authority to veto.

Conclude with a written pursuit decision and assigned next action. Reject opportunities requiring unlicensed representation, undisclosed self-dealing, unsupported authority, or cash advances outside policy. Keep unresolved documents visible with owners and dates rather than replacing them with optimistic assumptions.

fields.name: Initial county and service lane
fields.prompt: Define the initial geographic market, court, property segment, licensed activity, and concierge boundaries. Explain why the team can serve this lane without depending on unfamiliar procedures or speculative acquisition profits.
fields.example: Start with Sacramento County single-family probate listings priced from $450,000 to $800,000. The California supervising broker handles representation; the coordinator schedules estate-authorized vendors. Purchases by the operator require a separate conflict review and purchase file, and contribute nothing to the brokerage scorecard forecast.

fields.name: Candidate fit and leverage thesis
fields.prompt: Record the candidate's canonical rank, score components, and operating constraints. Identify the specific repetitive tasks that automation can remove while preserving licensed judgment and representative control over consequential decisions.
fields.example: Candidate #9, Probate Real Estate, ranks #16 of 29 with 76/100: revenue potential 23, margin potential 18, team efficiency 16, startup accessibility 9, and automation 10. Docket alerts and transaction checklists support the High-Leverage Operator Play; they do not replace court interpretation or negotiations.

fields.name: Representative identity and documented authority
fields.prompt: Identify the appointed representative, appointment date, current letters, relevant restrictions, and counsel's procedure assessment. Specify what evidence must exist before the broker accepts instructions, access permissions, or a listing agreement.
fields.example: Case PR-2026-0412 names Jordan Lee as personal representative. The file contains current Letters of Administration and the appointment order; counsel confirms full IAEA authority and checks for restrictions. Jordan signs the listing only after the broker verifies identity and matches the signing capacity.

fields.name: Counterparty communication and dispute map
fields.prompt: Map who instructs the broker, who receives updates, and who may object through the applicable procedure. Record actual disputes and communication permissions without assuming every beneficiary controls pricing or contract execution.
fields.example: Jordan instructs the broker; estate counsel receives legal questions; three beneficiaries receive an authorized Friday status summary. One beneficiary disputes the proposed cleanout budget. The broker records the concern and routes it to Jordan and counsel rather than collecting informal beneficiary signatures.

fields.name: Property condition and access underwriting
fields.prompt: Describe occupancy, utilities, security, insurance, deferred maintenance, and inspection access. Separate observed facts from estimates, identify qualified vendors, and assign the representative responsibility for authorizing estate expenditures.
fields.example: The $625,000 target property is vacant with active utilities and a leaking garage roof. Jordan authorizes a $450 inspection and obtains vacant-property coverage confirmation. The coordinator logs lockbox access; no belongings leave the house until the representative gives written disposition instructions.

fields.name: Title debt and estate proceeds bridge
fields.prompt: List preliminary liens, payoff estimates, taxes, selling costs, and title exceptions. Calculate illustrative estate proceeds separately from brokerage receipts, identifying items that require updated demands or title clearance before closing.
fields.example: At a $625,000 sale, subtract a $210,000 mortgage, $12,000 tax lien, $18,750 negotiated listing-side commission, and $14,250 other estimated selling costs: provisional estate proceeds equal $370,000. The operator retains $15,000 after the assumed brokerage split; payoff interest and final settlement charges remain subject to reconciliation.

fields.name: Sale route and court timing
fields.prompt: Identify whether the proposed transaction uses independent administration or a court-supervised sale route. Record counsel's required notices, objection handling, hearing dependencies, and timing assumptions rather than promising a fixed closing date.
fields.example: Counsel selects a full-authority IAEA sale subject to the applicable notice process under California Probate Code sections 10580–10589. The planning calendar allows notice time plus a 30-day buyer escrow. An objection moves the file to counsel's revised procedure before any closing commitment.

fields.name: Pricing evidence and downside sensitivity
fields.prompt: Document comparable sales, condition adjustments, valuation date, and the effect of a lower sale price on retained commission. State the negotiated rate and split explicitly; never present either as an industry requirement.
fields.example: Three adjusted comparable sales support $600,000 to $650,000, with $625,000 used for planning. At an illustrative negotiated 3% listing-side rate and 80% retention, operator revenue is $15,000. A 10% price reduction produces $562,500 of sale value and $13,500 of retained commission.

fields.name: Acquisition and concierge conflict screen
fields.prompt: Identify operator ownership interests, proposed purchases, vendor relationships, and concierge compensation. Describe how conflicts are disclosed and evaluated before proceeding, including alternatives that preserve independent representation and estate decision-making.
fields.example: An affiliated acquisition entity offers $540,000 while the listing analysis supports $625,000 before condition adjustments. The broker discloses ownership, stops using confidential seller leverage in acquisition negotiations, and asks counsel to assess the conflict and proposed procedure. The forecast excludes acquisition resale gains.

fields.name: Pursuit decision and resource ceiling
fields.prompt: State pursue, defer, or decline with evidence-based reasons, an initial labor budget, cash exposure limit, and next review date. Tie the decision to authority, economics, property readiness, and realistic closing dependencies.
fields.example: Pursue after authority verification, preliminary title review, and signed representation documents. Limit pre-listing work to 12 staff hours and $600 of brokerage spending; estate vendors invoice the estate directly. Review in seven days if access or insurance remains unresolved and defer marketing until those issues are cleared.

worksheets.completion_gate: The supervising broker records a pursuit decision supported by verified signing authority, a documented sale route, preliminary property and title findings, a retained-commission estimate, and named owners for every unresolved condition.

worksheets.title: Retained-Commission Economics, Defect Reserve, and Cash Float
worksheets.purpose: Reconcile the canonical revenue and owner-profit scenarios to retained brokerage commissions. Build a case-level cost bridge, an explicit failed-file allowance, and a cash timing plan that keeps estate money separate while exposing the funding gap created by delayed probate closings.
instructions: Enter all three canonical scenarios unchanged before adding local assumptions. Show sale value, gross listing-side commission, brokerage split, retained operator revenue, total costs, and owner net profit as separate quantities. Do not substitute property appreciation or acquisition proceeds for commissions.

Use negotiated commission and retention assumptions solely to construct a transparent unit model. Match annual retained revenue through closed-file counts, and distinguish realized closings from signed listings, pending escrows, and probability-weighted pipeline values that have not yet earned revenue.

Allocate recurring overhead, people costs, direct case costs, and failed-file allowances without counting any item twice. Explain which costs sit inside the monthly operating envelope and which require additional cash. Reconcile the complete annual expense total to the canonical margin.

Forecast cash by expected receipt and payment date rather than by annual averages alone. Stress a court delay and a reduced sale price separately. Never use estate deposits, trust funds, or vendor reimbursements to conceal the brokerage's own working-capital shortfall.

Set numerical hiring and spending conditions based on available unrestricted cash, committed funding, and documented costs. Keep launch capital separate from the mature team's annual economics, and show what happens when the first commission arrives near the far end of the timing range.

fields.name: Canonical scenario reconciliation
fields.prompt: Write the three annual revenue, margin, owner-profit, expense, and staffing combinations. Verify revenue multiplied by margin equals owner profit, and revenue less profit equals the complete implied expense envelope.
fields.example: Conservative: $120,000 revenue, 20% margin, $24,000 profit, $96,000 costs, 2 FT + 3 C. Base: $510,000 revenue, 27.5% margin, $140,250 profit, $369,750 costs, 2 FT + 3 C. Scaled: $900,000 revenue, 35% margin, $315,000 profit, $585,000 costs, 3 FT + 4 C.

fields.name: Sale value to retained commission bridge
fields.prompt: Calculate a representative closing from property sale value through negotiated listing-side commission and brokerage retention. Identify the recipient of each amount and the distinct recognition event for operator revenue.
fields.example: A $625,000 closing at an illustrative negotiated 3% listing-side commission generates $18,750 before the brokerage split. At 80% operator retention, $15,000 reaches the operator and $3,750 remains with the brokerage. Record the retained amount under the accountant's earned-revenue policy, not when the listing is signed.

fields.name: Annual closing count and property throughput
fields.prompt: Convert each scenario into an illustrative count of completed transactions. Reconcile aggregate property throughput separately from retained revenue, using explicit average prices, negotiated commission assumptions, and brokerage retention percentages.
fields.example: Conservative uses 10 closings at $500,000, producing $5,000,000 property throughput and $120,000 retained revenue at 3% commission and 80% retention. Base uses 34 closings at $625,000: $21,250,000 throughput and $510,000 revenue. Scaled uses 60 identical units: $37,500,000 throughput and $900,000 revenue.

fields.name: Base expense architecture and unit margin
fields.prompt: Build an illustrative expense schedule that sums exactly to the base expense envelope. Identify personnel, recurring overhead, case spending, and expected losses, then calculate fully allocated cost and profit per closing.
fields.example: Budget $108,000 recurring overhead, $216,000 people costs, $32,250 direct case spending, and $13,500 expected failed-file losses: total $369,750. People costs comprise $156,000 for two full-time roles and $60,000 across three contractors. Across 34 closings, cost is $10,875 and owner profit is $4,125 each.

fields.name: Scrub defects and failed-file allowance
fields.prompt: Define the events that consume the loss allowance, including duplicate leads, authority defects, abandoned listings, and unrecovered case spending. Separate an internal budgeting allowance from actual accounting treatment and restricted cash.
fields.example: Allocate the $13,500 management allowance as $3,000 for docket and identity rework, $4,500 for unrecovered inspection or marketing commitments, and $6,000 for abandoned-file labor. Review actual losses monthly. Moving $13,500 into a reserve account creates no second expense; the accountant controls recorded expense recognition.

fields.name: Startup capital and first-deal runway
fields.prompt: Place the launch plan within the canonical startup capital and first-deal ranges. Separate one-time setup from liquid runway and show the consequence of a late first closing without assuming the mature team already exists.
fields.example: Canonical startup capital is $15,000–$100,000 and time to first deal is 4–18 months. A $90,000 launch budget spends $15,000 on setup and leaves $75,000 liquid. A staged $6,000 monthly burn lasts 12.5 months; reaching month 18 requires another $33,000 or documented reductions before committing.

fields.name: Monthly operating envelope and mature float
fields.prompt: Explain how the quoted monthly operating range maps to this budget. Calculate mature-team cash requirements using all relevant costs rather than treating recurring overhead as the entire expense base.
fields.example: The canonical monthly opex range is $3,000–$18,000. For this worksheet, $9,000 is recurring non-personnel overhead, with $18,000 monthly people costs shown separately. Fixed cash demand is therefore $27,000 monthly, and 90 days requires $81,000 before direct case costs. This scope assumption must accompany the budget.

fields.name: Court-delay and price stress
fields.prompt: Stress delayed receipts and reduced sale prices without altering the canonical scenario labels. Quantify cash timing effects separately from profit effects, and state which cost assumptions remain fixed in the sensitivity.
fields.example: Moving two $15,000 commissions beyond the quarter creates a $30,000 receipt shortfall without automatically destroying lifetime revenue. Separately, a 10% price decline across 34 base closings reduces retained revenue to $459,000. Holding modeled costs at $369,750 leaves $89,250 profit; this is a sensitivity, not the canonical base.

fields.name: Break-even volume and contribution logic
fields.prompt: Separate fixed annual costs from variable case costs and expected losses. Calculate contribution per completed closing and the whole-number closing count required to cover fixed costs under the stated assumptions.
fields.example: Treat $324,000 of overhead and people costs as fixed. Allocate $45,750 of case spending and expected losses across 34 closings, or approximately $1,345.59 each. At $15,000 retained revenue, contribution is approximately $13,654.41. Fixed-cost break-even is 23.73 closings, rounded upward to 24 completed transactions.

fields.name: Cash ownership and funding decision
fields.prompt: Identify unrestricted brokerage cash, estate funds, trust deposits, proposed borrowing, and the next spending decision. Specify evidence required before treating future receipts or a credit facility as available working capital.
fields.example: The operator has $62,000 unrestricted cash against an $81,000 fixed-cost float target, leaving a $19,000 gap before case spending. A proposed $25,000 credit line counts only after execution and availability verification. Buyer earnest money remains with the authorized holder and cannot fund payroll or marketing.

worksheets.completion_gate: All canonical scenarios reconcile exactly; the base cost schedule totals $369,750; property throughput never appears as operator revenue; and the owner records a funded cash plan or specific spending reductions for the identified runway shortfall.

worksheets.title: Execution Ledger and Transaction QA Pre-Flight
worksheets.purpose: Turn a qualified probate opportunity into a controlled transaction file. Assign evidence, owners, and deadlines from intake through closing, preserve a clear commission ledger, and test the technical controls that prevent stale authority, premature marketing, misdirected funds, and incomplete handoffs.
instructions: Create a unique case identifier before importing documents or assigning tasks. Use the same identifier in the CRM, document folder, transaction checklist, and accounting reference. Keep sensitive identity and estate documents outside broadly shared prospecting views and marketing exports.

Define each transaction state by evidence rather than elapsed time. A signed listing does not prove authority remains current, a hearing date does not prove confirmation, and an accepted offer does not establish that required notices or objections have been resolved.

Assign one accountable owner for every deadline and one backup for absences. Record the source of each date and counsel's procedural instructions. Treat software reminders as operational aids, while preserving the underlying order, notice, contract, or verified court entry.

Reconcile the draft settlement statement to negotiated compensation, the brokerage split, and authorized credits. Verify payment instructions through a trusted independent channel. Keep estate distributions, buyer deposits, and operator receipts in separate ledger categories with explicit ownership.

Run a pre-closing review and a post-closing exception review. Test document access, duplicate prevention, deadline calculation, and receipt matching. Record failed checks with corrective actions and retest results rather than marking the entire file complete because funds were received.

fields.name: Case identity and source register
fields.prompt: Define the identifiers and source metadata needed to connect court records, property records, contacts, and transaction documents. Explain how duplicate estates and multiple properties belonging to one estate remain distinguishable.
fields.example: Use estate ID EST-0412 and property ID EST-0412-P01. Store the court case number, county, parcel number, source URL, and retrieval timestamp. A second property becomes P02 rather than a second estate. Match new imports on county plus case number before creating another representative contact.

fields.name: Evidence-based transaction states
fields.prompt: List the operational states and documentary requirements for moving between them. Include a suspended state for authority changes, objections, access failures, or contract issues that require review before further execution.
fields.example: States are prospect, authority review, engaged, preparation, active listing, under contract, closing ready, closed, and suspended. Engaged requires verified authority and executed representation documents. Closing ready requires counsel's procedure confirmation, title clearance, and escrow readiness. A new authority restriction moves the file to suspended immediately.

fields.name: Document custody and access matrix
fields.prompt: Specify where originals and working copies are stored, which roles can access sensitive material, and how version history is preserved. Define a narrow document-sharing procedure for vendors and external counterparties.
fields.example: Google Drive contains a restricted estate folder with separate authority, title, offers, and closing subfolders. The coordinator can manage checklists but cannot export identity documents. A cleanout vendor receives only the property address, access window, scope, and representative authorization through a limited-access folder.

fields.name: Deadline ledger and calendar validation
fields.prompt: Record each deadline's triggering event, source document, calculation method, owner, and backup. Explain how the team checks weekends, holidays, service rules, and amended orders before relying on a software date.
fields.example: The notice task records the notice document, counsel-approved service date, applicable objection period, and calculated earliest action date. The coordinator enters reminders seven and two days before review; the broker checks counsel's instructions. An amended order replaces the operative deadline while preserving the original audit entry.

fields.name: Vendor authorization and reimbursement ledger
fields.prompt: Document vendor scope, approving party, spending ceiling, invoice recipient, and completion evidence. Separate estate expenses from brokerage expenses and identify any reimbursement agreement before the operator advances funds.
fields.example: Jordan authorizes a $2,800 cleanout contract payable directly by the estate. The vendor supplies insurance evidence, before-and-after photographs, and an itemized invoice. The brokerage separately spends $450 on photography as its own marketing cost. Neither amount is added to retained commission revenue.

fields.name: Offer comparison and decision evidence
fields.prompt: Compare offers using net proceeds, funding evidence, contingencies, closing dependencies, and required court procedure. Record the representative's decision without allowing automated scoring to accept or reject a binding offer.
fields.example: Offer A is $625,000 with a 17-day inspection contingency and verified financing. Offer B is $610,000 cash with a seven-day inspection period. The broker prepares a net sheet for each and explains procedural dependencies. Jordan chooses A in writing after reviewing the documented tradeoffs.

fields.name: Closing commission and receipt reconciliation
fields.prompt: Tie the signed compensation terms to the settlement statement, brokerage disbursement, bank receipt, and accounting entry. Describe how credits, changed terms, or payment discrepancies remain visible until resolved.
fields.example: The closing statement shows $18,750 listing-side commission. The brokerage retains $3,750 and remits $15,000 to the operator. The coordinator matches the disbursement statement and bank receipt to EST-0412-P01; the bookkeeper records $15,000 retained revenue. A $250 discrepancy creates an exception, not an automatic revenue adjustment.

fields.name: Payment instruction verification control
fields.prompt: Define the independent verification procedure for changed payment instructions, including trusted contact sources, permitted communication channels, and stop conditions. Preserve proof of verification without exposing full account details in the CRM.
fields.example: An email requests a new escrow account two days before closing. The coordinator pauses the request and calls escrow using the number from the previously verified engagement record, not the email. The file records the verifier, callback time, and outcome; account details remain in the restricted closing folder.

fields.name: Technical pre-flight test cases
fields.prompt: Write concrete tests for duplicate records, missing authority, expired links, date changes, and reconciliation errors. Specify expected behavior and evidence so the team can repeat the tests after an automation change.
fields.example: Test five synthetic files: a repeated docket event creates no duplicate task; missing letters prevent engagement status; a vendor cannot open identity documents; a changed hearing date preserves history; and a $14,750 receipt against $15,000 expected creates a $250 exception. Save screenshots and the test-run date.

fields.name: Closing handoff and retained evidence
fields.prompt: Define the final deliverables, retention owner, open-item review, and post-closing follow-up. Identify what the broker may retain and what should be removed from marketing systems while preserving required transaction records.
fields.example: Within five business days, archive the executed agreement, authority evidence, required notices, settlement statement, commission reconciliation, and communications supporting material decisions. The broker applies California Business and Professions Code section 10148 and any longer applicable hold. Remove unnecessary identity attachments from the prospecting CRM and confirm outstanding invoices.

worksheets.completion_gate: The broker and coordinator complete the evidence checklist, resolve or formally assign every exception, demonstrate the five technical tests, and reconcile expected commission to the closing documents and actual bank receipt.

worksheets.title: Statutory, Licensing, Contract, and Outreach Audit
worksheets.purpose: Translate applicable licensing, fiduciary, sale-procedure, advertising, and outreach requirements into evidence the team can actually inspect. Use California as the worked jurisdiction, then replace its authorities when operating elsewhere instead of carrying one state's probate workflow into another court.
instructions: Identify the property jurisdiction and the court administering the estate before selecting statutes or forms. Have qualified local counsel confirm the sale route and material procedural requirements. Record citations, verification dates, and the transaction facts that make each requirement applicable.

Verify the supervising broker's license and each worker's permitted activity. Review representation, agency disclosures, compensation terms, vendor agreements, and acquisition conflicts before engagement. Administrative support must not drift into negotiation or other activity requiring a real estate license.

Build separate procedures for independent administration and court-supervised sales. Document required notices, objections, appraisal conditions, confirmation, and overbid mechanics where applicable. A CRM status label cannot establish that statutory prerequisites have been satisfied.

Audit attorney relationships and settlement-service referrals for prohibited compensation. Review outreach channels independently: postal mail, live calls, texts, automated calls, and commercial email have different requirements. Public court information does not create blanket permission to contact someone.

Convert every material issue into a correction with an owner and evidence deadline. Suspend the affected activity when authority, licensing, required procedure, or contact permission is missing. Preserve lawful work on other parts of the file while the issue is resolved.

fields.name: Jurisdiction and controlling procedure
fields.prompt: Identify the property location, probate court, administration type, and applicable procedural sources. State how the team verifies current local rules and distinguishes a general checklist from counsel's case-specific instructions.
fields.example: The property and probate proceeding are in Sacramento County, California. Counsel checks the appointment order, California Probate Code, and current Sacramento Superior Court probate rules. A property later identified in Nevada receives a separate jurisdiction review rather than inheriting California notice and sale assumptions.

fields.name: Broker licensing and worker scope
fields.prompt: Record license verification evidence and each role's permitted work. Identify who negotiates, signs brokerage documents, supervises advertising, and handles administrative tasks, citing the relevant licensing restriction for the worked jurisdiction.
fields.example: California Business and Professions Code section 10130 requires licensure for covered brokerage activity. The broker verifies active DRE status before assignment. The unlicensed coordinator schedules inspections and assembles documents but does not negotiate price or compensation. Compensation arrangements are checked against section 10137.

fields.name: Representative authority and fiduciary conflicts
fields.prompt: Document the representative's powers, restrictions, and potential interests in the buyer or vendors. Identify facts requiring counsel's review before a purchase, advance, or related-party arrangement proceeds.
fields.example: The representative proposes selling to a company they own. Counsel evaluates California Probate Code sections 9880–9885 and the specific facts before any commitment. The broker records ownership and alternative marketing evidence. A relationship disclosure alone is not treated as permission for a restricted transaction.

fields.name: IAEA notice and objection evidence
fields.prompt: For an independent-administration sale, record authority scope, required notice recipients, service evidence, objection handling, and any applicable waiver. Avoid assuming that full authority eliminates procedural notice or court involvement.
fields.example: Counsel confirms full authority and applies California Probate Code sections 10580–10589. The file contains the Notice of Proposed Action, recipient list, service evidence, and counsel's timing calculation, including the applicable minimum notice period. A timely objection halts the independent-action path pending counsel's instructions.

fields.name: Court-confirmed sale and overbid calculation
fields.prompt: For a sale requiring confirmation, record appraisal requirements, accepted price, hearing terms, and the statutory overbid calculation. Explain that meeting a numeric threshold does not itself secure court confirmation.
fields.example: For the applicable private sale, California Probate Code section 10309 requires at least 90% of appraised value, using an appraisal within one year. A $500,000 accepted bid has a $525,500 initial statutory overbid under section 10311: $1,000 on the first $10,000 plus $24,500 on the remainder.

fields.name: Agency disclosures and negotiated compensation
fields.prompt: Identify required agency disclosures, the client's signing capacity, compensation terms, and any dual-agency issue. Specify how the broker confirms the applicable documents and does not imply a mandatory commission rate.
fields.example: The California file uses applicable agency disclosures under Civil Code sections 2079.14–2079.17. The listing states an expressly negotiated 3% listing-side commission and identifies the representative's estate capacity. Any dual agency receives the required disclosure and consent, with Business and Professions Code section 10176(d) reviewed.

fields.name: Attorney referrals and settlement-service payments
fields.prompt: Describe every benefit exchanged with referral sources, including fees, gifts, shared marketing, and free services. Identify the transaction types requiring RESPA review and preserve evidence of genuine services rather than disguised referrals.
fields.example: The attorney relationship plan pays $0 for referrals. For transactions involving federally related mortgage loans, review 12 U.S.C. section 2607 and 12 CFR section 1024.14. A proposed $500 payment per referred closing is rejected. Genuine shared educational expenses require separate review of services, allocation, and other applicable rules.

fields.name: Calls texts and email channel controls
fields.prompt: Specify the outreach channel, recipient category, suppression checks, and any required permission. Distinguish manual business outreach from consumer telemarketing and automated messaging, with a documented process for honoring stop requests.
fields.example: Do not cold-text representatives from docket records. Consumer calling procedures address 47 U.S.C. section 227, 47 CFR section 64.1200, and applicable 16 CFR section 310.4 requirements, including registry screening. Commercial email follows 15 U.S.C. section 7704, including accurate headers, postal identification, and timely opt-out handling.

fields.name: Fair housing and property advertising
fields.prompt: Review listing copy, audience selection, offer handling, and lead segmentation for prohibited discrimination or misleading claims. Define objective property and service criteria that replace protected-characteristic proxies in marketing decisions.
fields.example: The broker reviews advertising under 42 U.S.C. section 3604 and California Government Code section 12955. Copy describes three bedrooms, step-free entry, and inspection access rather than preferred occupants. Audience selection uses service geography and property needs, not protected traits or inferred family characteristics.

fields.name: Data handling retention and correction register
fields.prompt: Record data categories, access controls, retention rules, privacy-law applicability, and corrective actions. Identify which public record details are unnecessary for outreach and should never enter a marketing export.
fields.example: Export only the minimum lawful contact and property fields; exclude identity documents, account numbers, and beneficiary medical details. Assess California Civil Code section 1798.100 et seq. applicability and section 1798.81.5 security duties. The broker owns retention review and corrects an overbroad vendor folder before restoring access.

worksheets.completion_gate: The supervising broker and appropriate local counsel have resolved the applicable authority, sale-procedure, licensing, contract, referral-payment, and outreach issues; evidence is linked to the file, and unresolved activities remain suspended.

worksheets.title: Automation Pipeline, Attorney Flywheel, and Risk Fallbacks
worksheets.purpose: Build a repeatable referral and execution system without turning court records into indiscriminate outreach. Combine authorized docket monitoring, structured qualification, useful attorney relationships, and transaction checklists with traceable data handling, measured conversion, and practical fallbacks for automation failures and disrupted sale timelines.
instructions: List authorized information sources and their access conditions before configuring ingestion. Prefer court-provided alerts or permitted licensed feeds. Record freshness, source identifiers, and retrieval errors so the CRM can distinguish new evidence from stale or duplicated records.

Automate collection, deduplication, reminders, and checklist preparation before automating outreach. Require qualified review for authority interpretation, procedural dates, pricing, offer decisions, and contractual commitments. Test with synthetic records before enabling any live workflow.

Build the attorney flywheel around useful estate-property work: valuation explanations, sale-route checklists, vendor coordination, and concise authorized updates. Measure relationships through qualified introductions and completed service, not payments or benefits contingent on referral volume.

Use a source-level funnel with explicit denominators and conversion windows. Separate newly created opportunities from prior-period closings. Show acquisition cost alongside staff capacity and cash timing so growth does not conceal an overloaded transaction pod.

Assign fallback owners for unavailable feeds, court postponements, family disputes, weak demand, and vendor outages. Define the operational trigger and immediate response for each. An automation failure must reduce convenience, not remove control over deadlines or client funds.

fields.name: Authorized docket source and freshness
fields.prompt: Identify the source, permitted access method, refresh cadence, and freshness threshold. Specify how the team verifies a docket event before using it to alter a transaction deadline or contact status.
fields.example: Use court-provided notifications where available or a licensed feed permitting the intended use. Refresh each business morning and flag records older than 48 hours. A new hearing event creates a review task; the coordinator checks the underlying entry before changing the operative calendar.

fields.name: CRM schema and deduplication rules
fields.prompt: Define the minimum record schema, stable identifiers, merge rules, and suppression links. Explain how the workflow handles repeated events without duplicating outreach, erasing provenance, or merging different people who share a name.
fields.example: Airtable stores county, case number, estate ID, parcel number, event ID, source timestamp, owner, and review status. County plus case number identifies the estate; contact merges require additional identity evidence. A normalized contact key links suppression preferences across all campaigns.

fields.name: Automation boundaries and review ownership
fields.prompt: List tasks the system may perform automatically and decisions reserved for a qualified person. Specify the owner and required evidence for each consequential status change or external communication.
fields.example: A Python job imports permitted docket events and creates draft tasks. It cannot mark authority verified, send consumer texts, accept offers, or release payment instructions. The broker confirms representation status; counsel supplies procedure guidance; the coordinator sends only reviewed, authorized updates.

fields.name: Attorney relationship value proposition
fields.prompt: Define a specific service promise for probate attorneys, the deliverables supporting it, and the relationship cadence. Exclude referral-contingent payments and avoid promising legal conclusions or a closing date outside the broker's control.
fields.example: Offer a two-business-day property intake response, a documented pricing analysis, and an authorized weekly sale-status summary. Meet eight probate attorneys during the first quarter to explain the process. Referrals earn no payment; service quality and reliable file updates create the reason to introduce another estate.

fields.name: Outbound cadence and suppression handling
fields.prompt: Describe the initial audience, message content, follow-up limit, and stop conditions. Make the channel-specific requirements visible and state how opt-outs propagate before another employee or tool sends a message.
fields.example: Send individually reviewed commercial emails to 20 relevant probate-law firms with a clear service description, postal address, and opt-out method. Permit one follow-up after ten business days. A stop request updates the central suppression list immediately and is checked before every later campaign.

fields.name: Base funnel and conversion assumptions
fields.prompt: Construct an illustrative annual funnel that reaches the base closing count. Identify the conversion denominator at each stage and state whether the model describes a mature pipeline or a newly launched business.
fields.example: A mature pipeline produces 200 qualified introductions, 100 consultations, 50 signed listings, and 34 closings annually. Stage conversions are 50%, 50%, and 68%; overall introduction-to-close conversion is 17%. At $15,000 retained per closing, revenue is $510,000. A new launch should not expect this annual output immediately.

fields.name: Attribution cost and acquisition payback
fields.prompt: Define source attribution, direct channel spending, labor allocation, and completed-deal measurement. Calculate a transparent acquisition cost without claiming that retained commission equals contribution or adding existing expenses a second time.
fields.example: Tag each introduction with its originating relationship and first-contact date. An illustrative $24,000 annual outreach allocation supporting 34 closings equals $705.88 per closing before separately allocated labor. The $24,000 already sits inside $108,000 overhead; do not add it again when reconciling base profit.

fields.name: Court delay and family dispute fallback
fields.prompt: Specify the trigger, owner, communication plan, and cash response for a postponed hearing or material family dispute. Identify what work stops and what property-protection tasks continue under valid authorization.
fields.example: A hearing moves by 60 days while a beneficiary challenges the sale. The coordinator moves the expected $15,000 receipt out of the current cash forecast. Counsel directs the procedural response; the broker pauses unsupported closing promises. Authorized insurance, security, and maintenance tasks continue with weekly updates.

fields.name: Housing-cycle response and capacity threshold
fields.prompt: Define measurable market and capacity triggers for adjusting pricing advice, spending, or intake volume. Preserve representative control over sale decisions and avoid treating increased leads as proof that the team can close more transactions.
fields.example: If median listing age exceeds 60 days or showings fall below two weekly for three weeks, the broker updates comparables and presents options to the representative. At more than 12 active files per coordinator, new intake slows until the broker verifies workload and funds additional capacity.

fields.name: Failure monitoring and manual recovery
fields.prompt: Document the automation health signals, alert recipient, recovery method, and replay controls. Specify how the team continues deadline review during an outage without creating duplicate tasks or unauthorized communications.
fields.example: A missing daily heartbeat by 10:00 a.m. alerts the coordinator. They review the authorized court source and the exported active-file deadline list manually. Recovery replays events using stable event IDs, creates no duplicate tasks, and requires a spot-check of five files before scheduled processing resumes.

worksheets.completion_gate: The pipeline has authorized sources, tested duplicate protection, central suppression handling, assigned review responsibilities, a base funnel that reconciles to 34 closings, and a demonstrated manual recovery path for docket and checklist outages.

worksheets.title: 30-Day Launch Sprint, Pod Scorecard, and Exit-Readiness Ledger
worksheets.purpose: Launch the operating system in 30 days without confusing setup progress with earned commissions. Define accountable roles, staged spending, measurable service quality, and transferable records that support a durable small-team brokerage while respecting the longer probate deal cycle.
instructions: Break the first month into four work packages with named owners and inspectable deliverables. Prioritize licensing, authority review, cash planning, and file controls before expanding outreach. Treat 30 days as an operating-system launch, not a promised closing deadline.

Assign work by licensed responsibility and actual capacity. Use the canonical staffing models as scenario references, but stage hiring against funded runway and case demand. A contractor label does not replace a worker-classification review or proper supervision.

Publish a weekly scorecard containing lead quality, authority readiness, file aging, service reliability, cash coverage, and realized retained revenue. Give every metric an owner, denominator, measurement period, and trigger that changes a specific operating decision.

Separate launch acceptance tests from mature economic targets. Demonstrate the workflow on synthetic records and then review authorized live cases. Record missed deliverables honestly and carry unresolved items into the next sprint with assigned dates and resources.

Build transferability from the first month: clean records, documented processes, reconciled receipts, permission-aware data exports, and a second person able to operate critical checklists. Do not assume client contracts, licenses, or referral relationships transfer automatically in a sale.

fields.name: Days 1–7 foundation package
fields.prompt: Assign the first week's jurisdiction, licensing, authority, budget, and workflow deliverables. Give each item an owner and objective acceptance evidence, including the conditions that prevent premature marketing or spending.
fields.example: By day 7, the broker verifies DRE status, selects Sacramento County, and reviews the representation packet. The coordinator creates the case template and access matrix. The owner approves the $90,000 launch plan and identifies the month-18 cash gap. No live listing begins without documented authority.

fields.name: Days 8–14 workflow and testing package
fields.prompt: Specify the second week's system configuration, synthetic cases, reconciliation tests, and recovery exercise. Define what must pass before staff use the workflow for live confidential documents or external communications.
fields.example: By day 14, create five synthetic cases and run duplicate, authority, access, deadline-change, and receipt-mismatch tests. Disable the docket importer for one exercise and complete manual review. The broker checks results; failed permissions tests block live document uploads until corrected and retested.

fields.name: Days 15–21 relationship and intake package
fields.prompt: Define the third week's target audience, reviewed outreach, meeting goals, and intake quality checks. Separate controllable activity targets from introductions or engagements that depend on independent counterparties choosing to respond.
fields.example: Prepare 20 reviewed law-firm contacts, send permitted individualized messages, and seek four introductory meetings. Actual meetings are reported separately from invitations. For each authorized estate introduction, the broker reviews authority and property fit before the coordinator creates a live transaction file.

fields.name: Days 22–30 launch acceptance package
fields.prompt: Define the final week's evidence review, cash check, service rehearsal, and next-month decision. Make launch completion independent of whether a commission has arrived, while keeping uncompleted deliverables visible.
fields.example: By day 30, the broker reviews all active files, the owner refreshes runway, and the coordinator rehearses the Friday client update. Accept launch only when critical controls pass. Record $0 earned commission if no closing occurred; the canonical first-deal expectation remains 4–18 months.

fields.name: Pod roles and staffing progression
fields.prompt: Assign the full-time and contractor responsibilities for the canonical scenarios. Explain how the launch stages capacity and how additional roles are authorized without assuming unpaid labor or automatic worker-classification outcomes.
fields.example: Conservative and base reference 2 FT + 3 C: licensed lead, transaction coordinator, and three specialist contractors. Scaled uses 3 FT + 4 C, seven people total, adding licensed capacity and another specialist. Launch starts lean; hiring requires funded costs, scope clarity, and applicable classification review.

fields.name: Weekly leading-indicator scorecard
fields.prompt: Specify leading metrics with targets, denominators, owners, and corrective actions. Prioritize qualified intake, evidence readiness, service timeliness, and capacity rather than raw contact counts or unsourced claims about pipeline value.
fields.example: The coordinator reports qualified introductions, consultations held, authority-ready files divided by engaged files, and on-time updates divided by updates due. Target 100% authority readiness and at least 95% timely updates. Two missed updates trigger a workload review before additional intake is assigned.

fields.name: Monthly realized-results scorecard
fields.prompt: Define the monthly revenue, cost, profit, cash, and closing metrics. Tie them to actual ledger evidence and show canonical annual comparisons without treating a monthly average as a predictable receipt schedule.
fields.example: Base annual targets are 34 closings, $510,000 retained revenue, $369,750 costs, and $140,250 owner profit. Arithmetic monthly averages are $42,500 revenue, $30,812.50 costs, and $11,687.50 profit. The dashboard shows actual receipts and earned revenue separately because probate closings do not arrive evenly.

fields.name: Thirty-day stop continue or adjust decision
fields.prompt: State the specific conditions for continuing, reducing spend, changing the service lane, or pausing new intake. Use evidence from runway, qualified demand, execution quality, and unresolved authority or licensing issues.
fields.example: Continue the county pilot when controls pass, outreach produces relevant conversations, and the next 90 days of committed spending are funded. Reduce discretionary spend if runway falls below six months before reliable receipts exist. Pause affected engagements immediately for unresolved authority or licensing defects.

fields.name: Exit-readiness evidence and transfer restrictions
fields.prompt: List the records a prospective successor would need to verify earnings, workflow, and client obligations. Identify restrictions on contract assignment, data sharing, licensing, and referral continuity before preparing any external diligence package.
fields.example: Maintain 24 months of reconciled retained-commission records when available, source attribution, documented procedures, vendor terms, and an exception log. A successor receives redacted summaries first. Counsel reviews assignment and confidentiality terms; the broker confirms licensing requirements. No valuation assumes that estate listings or attorney relationships transfer automatically.

fields.name: Key-person coverage and improvement ledger
fields.prompt: Identify critical tasks dependent on one person, name a qualified backup, and schedule a coverage exercise. Record improvement items with evidence, owners, and dates so transferability improves through tested operations rather than documentation alone.
fields.example: The broker is the only current negotiator, so qualified licensed coverage must be arranged before absence. The coordinator trains a permitted backup on deadline review and document permissions. A two-day coverage exercise tests five active-file tasks; any missed reminder receives an owner, correction date, and repeat test.

worksheets.completion_gate: The 30-day deliverables are evidenced, critical controls have passed their tests, the next spending period is funded or reduced to available resources, scorecard ownership is assigned, and the exit-readiness ledger distinguishes verified records from future evidence still to be accumulated.
